newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai gold trade looks to Indian Diwali.
newsitem.headline: Dubai gold trade looks to Indian Diwali.

text.p: Gold demand in Dubai is on a steady seasonal upturn but has yet to truly take-off before the start of the key Indian festival and wedding season, souk traders in the Gulf emirate said on Sunday.
Bullion demand was being helped by near year-low prices and early Indian buying ahead of the Hindu festival of Diwali that starts in November, market sources said.
Demand from Indian subcontinent expatriates in Dubai as well as from major Indian importers is expected to grow over the coming weeks to meet heightened seasonal gold demand there.
"As Diwali gets closer demand should be stronger for the next three to four months," a trader said.
Gold is also traditionally bought for celebrations during India's second major wedding season which runs from November through to April after farmers sell their crops.
The rupee's stability against the U.S. dollar and a Dubai-Bombay price difference of some 16 percent were also encouraging bullion and jewellery demand, traders said.
Dubai's benchmark Ten Tola bar (TT) -- 3.746 ounces of 24 carat gold -- was quoted by Dubai traders on Sunday at 5,265 UAE dirhams ($1,433.82), 10 dirhams higher on the week.
Ten gram pieces were quoted at 450 dirhams, up one dirham.
International spot bullion was last quoted on Sunday at $381.25/75, compared to a year-on-year $383.85.
"The price is considered to be quiet reasonable. At $380, buyers find it attractive," an expatriate souk trader said.
Dubai is the main feeder into India -- the world's singlest largest consumer of gold -- and an attractive market for tourists who are starting to visit the emirate in search of winter sun.

Of the estimated 28.8 tonnes of gold that imported into Dubai in August from major centres Switzerland and Britain, some 80 percent was re-exported to the subcontinent by official and unofficial carriers.
